questions.question: Find the value of x in given equation: (√(5 + x) + √(5 - x)) / (√(5 + x) - √(5 - x)) = 7
A gardener organizes trees into rows to create a square formation but discovers that 16 trees are not included. If the total number of trees is 4112 , then what is the number of trees in each row?
questions.explanation: Let n be the number of trees in each row. Total trees in square = 4112 - 16 = 4096. n² = 4096 => n = 64.

questions.question: The difference between the two numbers is 1370. On dividing the larger by the smaller, the quotient is 7, and the remainder is 14. Find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: Let smaller number = x, larger = 7x + 14. (7x + 14) - x = 1370 => 6x = 1356 => x = 226.

questions.question: Converting the decimal number 187 to the binary number system we get:
Which set of numbers includes all the other sets ?
questions.explanation: Real numbers include natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, and rational numbers.

questions.question: How many non-square natural numbers lie between 30² and 31²?
questions.explanation: For any two consecutive natural numbers n and (n+1), the number of non-square natural numbers between n² and (n+1)² is 2n. For n = 30: 2(30) = 60.

questions.question: What will be the number of zeros at the end of the square of the following numbers ? (i) 90 (ii) 600. Choose the correct option:

questions.explanation: Rational + Irrational is always Irrational. (5/3) + √5 is an irrational number.

questions.question: The five - digit number 45yz0 is divisible by 40. What is the maximum possible value of (y + z) ?
questions.explanation: 45yz0 is divisible by 40, so it must be divisible by 8 and 5. Divisibility by 8 requires the last three digits yz0 to be divisible by 8. For maximum (y + z), test y = 9, 8: when y = 8, z = 8, 880/8 = 110. y = 8, z = 8 => y + z = 16.

questions.question: In a room, there are some chairs and some people. If on each chair, only one person is seated, then there is no chair for exactly one person. If on each chair, two persons sit, then there is one vacant chair. What is the number of chairs in the room?
questions.explanation: Let chairs = x. 1 person per chair: people = x + 1. 2 persons per chair with 1 vacant chair: people = 2(x - 1). x + 1 = 2x - 2 => x = 3 chairs.

questions.question: Cindy bought 15 apples and 12 oranges and paid a sum of ₹447 for the purchase. Which of the statements given below is inconsistent with the information given in the previous statement, leading to no possible prices of the two fruits?

options.text: Purchased 25 apples and 20 oranges and paid a sum of ₹745
Purchased 10 apples and 13 oranges and paid a sum of ₹353
Purchased 12 apples and 8 oranges and paid a sum of ₹340
Purchased 35 apples and 28 oranges and paid a sum of ₹1,029

questions.explanation: 15A + 12O = 447 => 5A + 4O = 149. In (d), 35A + 28O = 7(5A + 4O) = 7(149) = 1043 ≠ 1029. This is inconsistent (parallel lines / no solution).

questions.question: Aman has certain number of notes of denomination ₹20 and ₹10 which amount to ₹390. If the numbers of notes of each kind are interchanged, then the new amount is ₹90 less than before. Find the number of notes of ₹20 denomination.

2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
questions.explanation: 2B + C = 69, 2C + 3F = 127, 3B + 4C + 2F = 229. Adding (i) and (iii): 5B + 5C + 2F = 298. Solving system yields F = 19. 5B + 5C + 5F = 298 + 3(19) = 355.

questions.question: 8 apples and 10 oranges weigh 5 kg. 12 apples and 20 oranges weigh 9 kg. What is the weight (in kg, rounded off to the nearest integer) of 15 apples and 24 oranges ?

In an election, voters have the option to vote for one of three candidates. They also have the option to select 'None Of The Above' (NOTA) to reject all the candidates. All three candidates get 6 times the NOTA votes. The winner gets twice the votes of the second runner-up. The first runner-up gets 900 more votes than NOTA and defeats the second runner-up by 150 votes. Find the total number of votes cast.
questions.explanation: Total votes cast for candidates = 6N. Winner W = 2R2, R1 = N + 900, R1 - R2 = 150 => R2 = N + 750. W = 2N + 1500. Total candidate votes = W + R1 + R2 = 4N + 3150 = 6N => 2N = 3150 => N = 1575. Total votes = 6N + N = 7N = 7(1575) = 11025.

questions.question: How many factors of 14,400 are divisible by 18 but not by 36 ?
questions.explanation: 14400 = 2⁶ × 3² × 5². Divisible by 18 (2 × 3²): 2^(1 to 6) × 3² × 5^(0 to 2). Not divisible by 36 (2² × 3²): powers of 2 must be exactly 1. Divisors = 1 × 1 × 3 = 3 factors.

questions.question: Raju has ₹11,000 and starts saving ₹5,000 each week towards buying a new laptop. At the same time, Ramesh has ₹60,000 and begins spending ₹2,000 per week on supplies for his art class. Will there be a week when they have the same amount of money?

options.text: No, they will never have the same amount

questions.question: If 3c2933k is divisible by both 5 and 11, where c and k are single digit natural numbers, then c + k = ______.
questions.explanation: 3c2933k divisible by 5 and 11. Natural number k = 5. Alternating sum: (3 + 2 + 3 + 5) - (c + 9 + 3) = 13 - (c + 12) = 1 - c. For divisibility by 11, 1 - c = 0 => c = 1. c + k = 1 + 5 = 6.

Find the lowest positive value of (c – b) such that the 7-digit number 1738b9c is divisible by 12.
questions.explanation: 1738b9c divisible by 12 (3 and 4). Last two digits 9c divisible by 4: c can be 2 or 6. Sum of digits = 28 + b + c. For least positive (c - b): if c = 6, b = 5 (28 + 11 = 39, div by 3), c - b = 6 - 5 = 1.

Ram gives a six-digit number 468312 to Shyam to check the divisibility. Shyam tells Ram that the number is divisible by 57. Shyam asks Ram, “If we rearrange the digits of this number in descending order, then by which number will it be always divisible ?”
questions.explanation: Sum of digits of 468312 = 4 + 6 + 8 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 24 (divisible by 3). Rearranging digits does not change the sum of digits, so it will always be divisible by 3.

questions.question: A 4-digit number '34PQ' divisible by 3, 5 and 7. Find the value of P + Q .
A six-digit number is divisible by 33. If 21 is added to the number, then the new number which formed is also divisible by:
questions.explanation: Divisible by 33 => divisible by 3. Since 21 is a multiple of 3, the sum (number + 21) is also divisible by 3.

questions.question: A six-digit number 11p9q4 is divisible by 24. Then the greatest possible value for pq is:
questions.explanation: 11p9q4 divisible by 24 (3 and 8). 9q4 divisible by 8 => q = 4 or 8 (largest q = 8). For q = 8: sum of digits = 1 + 1 + p + 9 + 8 + 4 = 23 + p divisible by 3 => max p = 7. pq = 7 × 8 = 56.

questions.question: The remainder of the term 9 + 9² + .... + 9^(2n + 1) when divided by 6 is:
questions.explanation: 9 ≡ 3 (mod 6). Any power 9^k ≡ 3 (mod 6). Sum of (2n + 1) terms: (2n + 1) × 3 = 6n + 3 ≡ 3 (mod 6). Option (b) or (d) Answer key says (d).

The six-digit number 7x1yyx is a multiple of 33 for non-zero digits x and y. Which of the following could be a possible value of (x + y) ?
questions.explanation: 7x1yyx divisible by 33 (3 and 11). (7 + 1 + y) - (x + y + x) = 8 - 2x = 0 => x = 4. Divisible by 3: 7 + 4 + 1 + 2y + 4 = 16 + 2y is multiple of 3 => y = 1. x + y = 4 + 1 = 5.

questions.question: A girl wants to plant trees in her garden in rows in such a way that the number of trees in each row to be the same. There are 10 rows and the number of trees in each row is 12, what is the number of trees in each row, if there are 5 more rows ?
questions.explanation: Total trees = 10 × 12 = 120. With 15 rows: trees per row = 120 / 15 = 8.

questions.question: If the seven-digit number 52A6B7C is divisible by 33, and A, B, C are primes, then the maximum value of 2A + 3B + C is:
questions.explanation: 52A6B7C divisible by 33. Difference of alternating digits: (5+A+B+C) - (2+6+7) = A+B+C - 10 = 0 => A+B+C = 10. Prime trio summing to 10: {2, 3, 5}. Max 2A + 3B + C with B = 5, A = 3, C = 2 is 2(3) + 3(5) + 2 = 23.

questions.question: In a test (+ 5) marks are given for every correct answer and (−2) marks are given for every incorrect answer. Jay answered all the questions and scored (−12) marks, though he got 4 correct answers. How many of his answers were INCORRECT ?
questions.explanation: Correct = 4 × 5 = 20. Total score = -12. Marks lost = 20 - (-12) = 32. Incorrect answers = 32 / 2 = 16.

questions.question: The number 150328 is divisible by 23. If the digits are rearranged in descending order and five times of 13 is subtracted from the new number thus formed, then the resultant number will be divisible by:

questions.question: What is the sum of all the common terms between the given series S1 and S2 ? S1 = 2, 9, 16, ……., 632; S2 = 7, 11, 15, ……., 743
questions.explanation: Common difference = LCM(7, 4) = 28. First common term = 23. Last term <= 632: 23 + 28(n - 1) <= 632 => n = 22. Sum = (22/2)[2(23) + 21(28)] = 6974.

questions.question: Let p, q, r and s be positive natural numbers having three exact factors including 1 and the number itself. If q > p and both are two-digit numbers, and r > s and both are one-digit numbers, then the value of the expression (p - q - 1)/(r - s) is:
questions.explanation: Numbers with exactly 3 factors are squares of primes: {4, 9, 25, 49}. Two-digit: q = 49, p = 25. One-digit: r = 9, s = 4. (p - q - 1)/(r - s) = (25 - 49 - 1)/(9 - 4) = -25/5 = -5 = -4 - 1 = -s - 1.
